mainTopic: How a ספר תורה ends, the reading of its last eight פסוקים, the value of writing one, and the rules for laying out its columns and margins
overview: The amud opens by finishing the previous discussion: extra letters in a ספר תורה are not a problem. The גמרא then brings רב's ruling that a ספר תורה may end in the middle of a column. After a challenge from a ברייתא, the גמרא explains that רב meant the ends of the חומשין inside the scroll, and that the very end of the תורה may stop in the middle of a line. The הלכה follows רב אשי: the תורה must end specifically in the middle of the last line. Next comes רב's rule that the last eight פסוקים of the תורה are read by one person. The גמרא ties this to the מחלוקת over whether יהושע wrote them or משה wrote them with tears. It concludes that the rule fits both views. רב then teaches that writing a ספר תורה yourself is like receiving it at סיני, and רב ששת adds that correcting even one letter counts as writing it. Finally a ברייתא lays out the scroll: columns per sheet, line width, margins, and the spaces between lines, words and letters. It also forbids shrinking the writing to save space and splitting a word into the margin.

steps.title: Extra letters are not a problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the previous discussion. Extra letters in a ספר תורה do not cause the problem that was being discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But extra letters, we have no problem with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the previous discussion about mistakes in a ספר תורה. It says that extra letters are not a concern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rule was about errors that are hard to fix. Extra letters can simply be erased, so they are left out of that concern. This line closes the first of רב's two rulings, the one that was refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: Extra letters, written beyond the correct spelling
We have no problem with it

phrases.english: But extra letters, we have no problem with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous part of the daf
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The concern about errors applies to missing letters, not to extra letters.

steps.title: רב rules that a סופר may finish a ספר תורה even mid-column
steps.stepSummary: This is רב's second ruling: a סופר finishing a ספר תורה may finish anywhere, even in the middle of a column.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other ruling is what רב said: one who writes a ספר תורה and comes to finish it may finish, even in the middle of the column.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings the second of רב's two rulings. It is about where the last words of a ספר תורה may be written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the end of a ספר תורה must fill the column to the very bottom. רב says there is no such requirement, and the סופר may stop even partway down the column.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one (here, רב's second ruling)
A Torah scroll
To finish writing
A column of writing in the scroll

phrases.english: The other one is that which רב said:
phrases.notes: Earlier the גמרא said רב made two rulings that a ברייתא challenged. This is the second one.

phrases.english: One who writes a Torah scroll and comes to finish it
may finish, and even in the middle of the column.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the second of רב's two rulings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סופר may finish a ספר תורה even in the middle of a column.

steps.title: A ברייתא says not to finish mid-column
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a ספר תורה may not end mid-column. Instead the סופר narrows the lines so the writing reaches the bottom of the column.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: One who writes a ספר תורה and comes to finish may not finish in the middle of the column, the way one finishes a single חומש. Rather, he keeps shortening the lines until the end of the column.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב with a ברייתא that says the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא contrasts two cases. A single חומש written alone may end mid-column, but a full ספר תורה must end at the bottom. To make the writing come out right, the סופר shortens the lines as he goes.

keyTerms.meaning: Single books of the תורה, each written as its own scroll
Keeps shortening (the width of the lines)
The bottom of the column

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'חומשין' means single books of the תורה written as separate scrolls, not a printed חומש.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: One who writes a Torah scroll,

phrases.aramaic: בָּא לוֹ לִגְמוֹר – לֹא יִגְמוֹר בָּאֶמְצַע הַדַּף
phrases.english: and comes to finish, may not finish in the middle of the column
the way one finishes single books of the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מְקַצֵּר וְהוֹלֵךְ עַד סוֹף הַדַּף!
phrases.english: rather he keeps shortening the lines until the end of the column!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a ספר תורה may end mid-column
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly forbids ending a ספר תורה mid-column. It allows that only for a single חומש.

steps.title: רב was talking about חומשין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב's ruling was said about חומשין, not about the end of the whole ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב said it, he was talking about חומשין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by limiting his ruling to חומשין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב meant חומשין, he agrees with the ברייתא, which also allows a חומש to end mid-column. The contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: When he said it (he meant this case)

phrases.english: When רב said it, it was about single books of the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב was talking about finishing a full ספר תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב was talking about finishing a חומש.

steps.title: But רב said 'ספר תורה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: רב's words clearly say 'ספר תורה', not חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he said 'a ספר תורה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that the answer does not fit רב's actual words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's ruling opened with 'הכותב ספר תורה'. Saying he meant a separately written חומש seems to go against his own wording.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it that (introduces a challenge)
He is saying

phrases.english: But he is talking about a Torah scroll?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רב meant חומשין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's own words say ספר תורה, so he cannot have meant a separate חומש.

steps.title: The חומשין inside a ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא clarifies that רב meant the ends of the חומשין inside a full ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He meant the חומשין that are part of a ספר תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens its answer. רב was talking about where each book ends inside a complete ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside a ספר תורה, the end of בראשית, שמות, ויקרא or במדבר may fall mid-column. This fits both רב's words ('ספר תורה') and the ברייתא, which only requires the very end of the whole תורה to reach the bottom.

keyTerms.meaning: The individual books inside a complete Torah scroll

steps.whatToRemember: Within a ספר תורה, the first four books may end mid-column. The question is only about the end of the whole תורה.

phrases.english: About the single books that are part of a Torah scroll.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5
steps.terutzMaskana: 'חומשין' means the books within a full ספר תורה.

steps.title: רב also said the end of the תורה may be mid-column
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another statement of רב: 'לעיני כל ישראל', the last words of the תורה, may be written in the middle of the column.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי יהושע בר אבא said in the name of רב גידל in the name of רב: 'לעיני כל ישראל' in the middle of the column?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new explanation with another ruling of רב himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב apparently allowed the very last words of the whole תורה to end mid-column. So he really does seem to argue with the ברייתא, and limiting him to the inner חומשין no longer works.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (introduces a challenge)
'Before the eyes of all Israel', the final words of the תורה

phrases.aramaic: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Is that so? But didn't רבי יהושע בר אבא say
that רב גידל said that רב said:
'In the sight of all Israel' may be in the middle of the column?
phrases.notes: דברים 34:12, the very last words of the תורה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation from step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that רב only meant the inner חומשין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב explicitly allowed the end of the whole תורה to be mid-column, which contradicts the ברייתא.

steps.title: That ruling meant the middle of the line
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב's ruling about 'לעיני כל ישראל' was about the middle of the line, not the middle of the column.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ruling was said about the middle of the line.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that this ruling of רב was really about ending in the middle of a line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The column still ends at the bottom, as the ברייתא requires. The last line, however, may stop in the middle instead of stretching across the full width. So there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: A line of writing

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two 'middles' apart. אמצע הדף means partway down the column. אמצע שיטה means partway across a line.

phrases.english: That one was said about the middle of the line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling allowed the תורה to end partway down the column.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling allows the last line to end partway across.

steps.title: רבנן and רב אשי disagree about ending mid-line
steps.stepSummary: רבנן say the תורה may end even in the middle of a line. רב אשי says it must end specifically in the middle of a line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן say: even in the middle of a line. רב אשי says: specifically in the middle of a line.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a disagreement about how to understand the rule of ending in the middle of a line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבנן, ending mid-line is allowed, but ending at the end of the line is fine too. For רב אשי, ending mid-line is required.

keyTerms.meaning: Even (allowed, but not required)
Specifically, only this way

phrases.english: The Rabbis say: even in the middle of the line,

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: בְּאֶמְצַע שִׁיטָה דַּוְוקָא,
phrases.english: רב אשי says: specifically in the middle of the line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the mid-line ruling from step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבנן: mid-line is permitted. רב אשי: mid-line is required.

steps.title: The הלכה: specifically mid-line
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רב אשי: the ספר תורה must end specifically in the middle of the line.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: specifically in the middle of the line.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute is decided in favor of רב אשי. The last words of the תורה must stop partway across the final line, while the column still reaches the bottom.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical הלכה

steps.whatToRemember: A ספר תורה ends at the bottom of the column, with the last line ending in the middle. Inner חומשין may end mid-column.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the actual practice for how a סופר lays out the end of every ספר תורה.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: specifically in the middle of the line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute in step 9
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ספר תורה must end specifically in the middle of the line, like רב אשי.

steps.title: The last eight verses are read by one person
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the last eight פסוקים of the תורה are read by a single individual in בית הכנסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בר אבא said in the name of רב גידל, who said in the name of רב: the eight פסוקים of the תורה are read by one person in the בית הכנסת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement of רב. The last eight פסוקים of the תורה must be read by one person, not split up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the קריאת התורה can be divided between readers at many points. רב says these eight פסוקים are a single unit that may not be broken up. The reason is not given yet. The next steps will show what it depends on.

keyTerms.meaning: Eight verses: the last eight פסוקים of the תורה, starting from משה's death
One individual reads them; the section is not split between readers
Synagogue, where the תורה is read publicly

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua bar Abba said,
Rav Giddel said, Rav said:
The eight verses in the Torah,
phrases.notes: He means the last eight פסוקים, which begin with משה's death.

phrases.english: one individual reads them in the synagogue.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the end of a ספר תורה (where it ends on the line) to how its last eight פסוקים are read.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The last eight פסוקים of the תורה are read in full by one person and not divided.

steps.title: Whose opinion does רב follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא רב's ruling follows and answers: not רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom is this? Not according to רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose view רב is following and gives a short answer: not רבי שמעון's. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling only makes sense if these eight פסוקים are different from the rest of the תורה. At first the גמרא assumes that רבי שמעון does not see them as different, so רב would follow the other opinion, which the ברייתא will show. Step 17 later shows that the ruling can fit רבי שמעון as well.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? It asks which earlier sage a ruling follows
Not in agreement with...

phrases.english: According to whom?
Not according to Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies which side of a תנאים dispute רב's ruling depends on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view does רב's ruling follow?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not רבי שמעון's; by implication, רבי יהודה's (or רבי נחמיה's).

steps.title: רבי יהודה: יהושע wrote the last eight verses
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי יהודה's view: משה could not have written about his own death, so יהושע wrote the last eight פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: "And משה the servant of ה׳ died there." Could משה have been alive and written "And משה died there"? Rather, משה wrote up to this point, and from here on יהושע בן נון wrote. These are the words of רבי יהודה, and some say רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains רב's ruling. רבי יהודה says the last eight פסוקים were written by יהושע, not משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה asks how משה could write that he died while he was still alive. So he concludes that יהושע wrote the פסוקים from משה's death onward. Since this section had a different writer, it stands as its own unit, so one person reads all of it.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
Is it possible? A way of showing something cannot be
Up to here... from here onward; it splits the text into two parts

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for רב's ruling. Because the last eight פסוקים had a different writer, they are treated as one separate unit in the public reading.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
"And Moses the servant of the Lord died there,"
is it possible that Moses was alive
and wrote "And Moses died there"?
Rather, until here Moses wrote,

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ כָּתַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן,
phrases.english: from here onward Joshua bin Nun wrote;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda,
and some say it was Rabbi Nechemya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source showing the view that רב follows.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that one person reads the last eight פסוקים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבי יהודה (or רבי נחמיה) says יהושע wrote these פסוקים

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the ספר תורה was not missing anything
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון objects that the ספר תורה could not have been missing even one letter in משה's lifetime, since משה was told to place the finished scroll by the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said to him: Is it possible that the ספר תורה was missing even one letter? But it is written: "Take this ספר תורה and place it, etc."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון challenges רבי יהודה. He says the תורה must have been complete while משה was alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of "this ספר תורה" being put in place in משה's lifetime. That implies it was already finished. If יהושע added eight פסוקים later, the scroll would have been incomplete, so רבי יהודה's view cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: Missing a single letter
But it is written: brings a פסוק to challenge an idea
This ספר תורה: the scroll משה gave over, complete

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֶפְשָׁר סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה חָסֵר אוֹת אַחַת?
phrases.english: Is it possible that the Torah scroll was missing even one letter?
But it is written: "Take this Torah scroll
and place it, etc."
phrases.notes: "This" scroll was put in place while משה was alive, so it was already whole.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: אֶפְשָׁר סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה חָסֵר אוֹת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יהודה's claim from the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim that יהושע wrote the last eight פסוקים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק shows the ספר תורה was complete in משה's lifetime, so nothing could have been added after his death.

steps.title: משה wrote the last verses with tears
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains that משה wrote the whole תורה. For the last eight פסוקים he wrote with tears and did not repeat the words, like ברוך writing for ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, up to here ה׳ said the words and משה wrote and repeated them aloud. From here on ה׳ said the words and משה wrote with tears, as it says elsewhere: "And ברוך said to them: From his mouth he would call out all these words to me, and I would write them in the book with ink."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives his own answer to רבי יהודה's question. משה did write about his own death, but in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For most of the תורה, ה׳ said the words and משה wrote them and repeated them aloud. For the last eight פסוקים, משה only wrote while ה׳ said them, and he wrote crying. The פסוק about ברוך is a case where one person dictates and the other just writes. So for רבי שמעון the תורה was complete in משה's lifetime, and משה wrote these פסוקים too. Step 16 will ask whether that means רב's ruling cannot follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: Writes and says: משה wrote the words and repeated them aloud
With tears
As it says elsewhere: brings a parallel פסוק
Ink

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה says יהושע wrote the last eight פסוקים. רבי שמעון says משה wrote everything, and the last part he wrote with tears, without repeating the words aloud.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not say these eight פסוקים are different in who wrote them. Only the way משה wrote them changed. Step 17 will use exactly this difference to show that רב's ruling can fit רבי שמעון too.

phrases.english: Rather, until here,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, would say the words
and Moses would write and say them aloud;
from here onward,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, would say the words
and Moses would write with tears,
as it is stated elsewhere:
"And Baruch said to them:
From his mouth he would call out to me
all these words,
and I would write them in the book with ink."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, עַד כָּאן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אוֹמֵר וּמֹשֶׁה כּוֹתֵב וְאוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי שמעון answers רבי יהודה's original question without having יהושע write anything.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the change at משה's death was in the way of writing, not in who wrote.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה could not have written about his own death, so יהושע must have written it (רבי יהודה).
steps.terutzMaskana: ה׳ dictated and משה wrote with tears without repeating the words, so the ספר תורה was complete in משה's lifetime.

steps.title: Does רב's rule go against רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב's rule fits only רבי יהודה and not רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב's ruling does not follow רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the מחלוקת it just quoted: maybe רב's rule cannot fit רבי שמעון. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, יהושע wrote the last eight פסוקים, so it makes sense that they are read as a separate unit. According to רבי שמעון, משה wrote them like the rest of the תורה, so why should they be treated differently? That would mean רב's rule fits only רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It opens a suggestion that the גמרא may reject.

phrases.english: Shall we say that it is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon?
phrases.notes: "It" means רב's rule that one person reads the last eight פסוקים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion that the ברייתא in steps 13-15 seemed to point toward.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי שמעון, משה wrote these פסוקים like all the others, so there seems to be no reason to read them differently.

steps.title: It can fit רבי שמעון: they were already different
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי שמעון agrees that the last eight פסוקים are special, because משה wrote them differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say רב follows רבי שמעון. Since these פסוקים are different in one way, they are different in this way too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב's rule works even according to רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, משה wrote the last eight פסוקים with tears and without repeating the words aloud. Since they already stand apart in how they were written, they also stand apart in how they are read. So one person reads them without a break.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. It shows the rule fits the other view too.
Since they are different, they are different. Something special in one way can be special in another way too.

steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule (one reader for the last eight פסוקים) works according to both רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Shimon:
since they are different, they are different.
phrases.notes: They were written differently, with tears and without repeating (step 15). So they are also read differently.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling fits both views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only רבי יהודה, who says יהושע wrote them, would treat these פסוקים as a separate unit.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי שמעון too they are special, because משה wrote them in a special way. So they are read as one unit.

steps.title: Buying a ספר תורה versus writing one
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that buying a ספר תורה is like grabbing a מצוה, but writing one is like receiving it at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who buys a ספר תורה in the market is like someone who grabs a מצוה in the market. If he writes it, the פסוק treats him as if he received it at הר סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רב, passed down through two other sages, about how much the מצוה of a ספר תורה is worth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Buying a ready-made ספר תורה is the less ideal way to do the מצוה. The best way is to write it yourself. Then he is treated as if he personally received the תורה at סיני.

keyTerms.meaning: One who buys
Grabbing a מצוה, getting it the easy way rather than the ideal way
The פסוק counts it for him as if...

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for how important it is to write a ספר תורה yourself, not just to own one.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua bar Abba said
that Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
One who buys a Torah scroll from the market
is like one who grabs a מצוה from the market;
if he wrote it himself,
the verse counts it for him
as if he received it at Mount Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching from רב about the ספר תורה, following his earlier teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Writing a ספר תורה yourself is the ideal way to do the מצוה. Buying one is less ideal.

steps.title: Correcting one letter counts as writing it
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת adds that correcting even a single letter in a ספר תורה counts as writing the whole scroll.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he corrected even one letter, it is counted for him as if he wrote it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת adds to רב's teaching and shows a way to get credit for writing a ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You do not have to write the entire scroll yourself. Fixing even one letter makes the scroll usable, and that earns the same credit as writing it.

keyTerms.meaning: Corrected, fixed a mistake in the text
One letter

steps.whatToRemember: Writing a ספר תורה is like receiving it at סיני, and correcting even one letter counts as writing it.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
If he corrected even one letter,
it is counted for him as if he wrote it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to רב's teaching in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Correcting even one letter of a ספר תורה earns the credit of writing it.

steps.title: A sheet must have three to eight columns
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that each sheet of parchment in a ספר תורה should have between three and eight columns.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory sign: סגל"ם.) רבנן taught: A person may make a sheet with anywhere from three columns up to eight columns. He should not make one with fewer or more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a memory sign and then starts a new ברייתא about how to lay out the sheets of a ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ספר תורה is made of sheets of parchment sewn together. The ברייתא sets a range for how many columns of writing go on each sheet: at least three and at most eight.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign that hints at the coming teachings
A sheet of parchment, one of the pieces sewn together to make the scroll
Columns of writing

phrases.english: (Memory sign: Samekh, Gimmel, Lamed, Mem)
The Rabbis taught:
A person may make a sheet
from one of three columns
up to one of eight columns;
less than this or more than this
he should not make.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the rules for the layout of a ספר תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each sheet of a ספר תורה should have between three and eight columns.

steps.title: Columns should be neither too narrow nor too wide
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: columns should not be too many and narrow or too few and wide. The ideal width fits למשפחותיכם three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should not make too many columns, because then it looks like a letter. He should not make too few columns, because then the reader's eyes wander. Rather, a line should be wide enough to write "למשפחותיכם" three times.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the reasons for the column rules and gives a measure for the ideal width of a line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Too many columns on a sheet makes them narrow, so the scroll looks like a short letter instead of a ספר תורה. Too few columns makes the lines so long that the reader loses his place. The ideal line fits the word למשפחותיכם three times.

keyTerms.meaning: A letter (a written message), which has short, narrow lines
His eyes wander, so he loses his place in a long line
"For your families", the word used to measure the ideal width of a line

steps.confusionAlert: "Too many" and "too few" columns is really about column width. More columns on a sheet means narrower columns, and fewer columns means wider ones.

phrases.english: And he should not make too many columns,
because it looks like a letter,
phrases.notes: Many columns means narrow columns, like the short lines of a letter someone sends.

phrases.english: and he should not make too few columns,
because his eyes wander;
rather, for example,
"lemishpechoteichem, lemishpechoteichem, lemishpechoteichem"
phrases.notes: The line should be wide enough to fit this word written three times.

phrases.english: three times.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יַרְבֶּה בְּדַפִּין מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה אִגֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 20 and explains the reasons behind its range.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Columns should not be too narrow or too wide. The ideal line fits למשפחותיכם three times.

steps.title: Splitting a nine-column sheet evenly
steps.stepSummary: If a sheet has nine columns, too many for one sheet, split it four and five, not three and six.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone ends up with a sheet that has nine columns, he should not split it into three columns and six columns. He should split it into four and five.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its rule about how many columns go on each sheet. It covers a sheet with nine columns, one more than the maximum of eight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said a sheet holds three to eight columns, so nine is too many and the sheet must be split. Three and six would both be allowed, but the ברייתא wants the two sheets close in size, so it says four and five.

keyTerms.meaning: A sheet of parchment; many sheets are sewn together to make the scroll
Columns of writing on a sheet (singular: דַּף)
He should not divide it

phrases.aramaic: נִזְדַּמְּנָה לוֹ יְרִיעָה בַּת תֵּשַׁע דַּפִּים,
phrases.english: If he happened to have a sheet of nine columns,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַחְלוֹק שָׁלֹשׁ לְכָאן וְשֵׁשׁ לְכָאן,
phrases.english: he should not divide it three here and six here,
but rather four here and five here.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִזְדַּמְּנָה לוֹ יְרִיעָה בַּת תֵּשַׁע דַּפִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's column rules with a practical case of a sheet that is too long.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nine-column sheet is split into four and five columns so the two sheets are close in size.

steps.title: The last sheet of the scroll may be short
steps.stepSummary: The three-column minimum applies only before the end of the scroll. The last sheet can be much smaller.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this rule apply? At the beginning of the scroll. But at the end of the scroll, a sheet may hold even one verse and even one column.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא limits its own rule. The minimum of three columns per sheet does not apply to the final sheet of the scroll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from Step 20 that each sheet needs at least three columns is said about the beginning of the scroll. At the end, the writer may finish with a very small sheet. The wording 'even one verse' will bother the גמרא in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case was this said? This phrase introduces a limit on an earlier rule
The beginning of the scroll
The end of the scroll

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: This points back to the rule that a sheet needs at least three columns.

phrases.english: At the beginning of the scroll,
but at the end of the scroll —

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ פָּסוּק אֶחָד וַאֲפִילּוּ דַּף אֶחָד.
phrases.english: even one verse and even one column.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the column rules: the final sheet is an exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The minimum of three columns does not apply to the last sheet of the scroll.

steps.title: Can a whole sheet be just one verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: it makes no sense for a sheet to hold only a single verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can it really enter your mind that a sheet holds just one verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording 'even one verse' in the ברייתא. This sets up a corrected reading in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken literally, the ברייתא says a whole sheet could contain only one verse. The גמרא finds that impossible, so the wording must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? The גמרא uses this to reject a reading as impossible

phrases.english: One verse, can it enter your mind?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the literal wording of the ברייתא in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'even one verse' in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read literally, a sheet would hold only one verse, which cannot be correct.

steps.title: Read it as one verse in one column
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording: the last sheet can be a single column, even if that column holds only one verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: one verse in one column.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by rereading the ברייתא. The two phrases 'one verse' and 'one column' describe one case together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two 'even' phrases do not describe two separate cases. They describe one case: the last sheet can have a single column, and that column may hold as little as one verse.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say: the גמרא is correcting how the text should be read

steps.whatToRemember: The three-to-eight column rule has an exception at the end of the scroll: the last sheet may be one column, even with only one verse in it.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
one verse in one column.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 24 by rereading the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A sheet could contain only a single verse.
steps.terutzMaskana: The last sheet can be a single column, even if that column holds only one verse.

steps.title: How wide the margins must be
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives the margin sizes for a full ספר תורה and the smaller sizes for a single חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The size of the margin: at the bottom, a טפח; at the top, three fingers; and between columns, the width of two fingers. In separate חומשים: at the bottom, three fingers; at the top, two fingers; and between columns, the width of a thumb.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves from columns to margins. It gives the size of the bottom, top and side spaces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full ספר תורה gets bigger margins: a טפח at the bottom, three fingers at the top, and two fingers between columns. A single חומש written as its own scroll gets smaller ones: three fingers, two fingers, and a thumb. The bottom margin is always the largest.

keyTerms.meaning: The margin, the blank parchment around the writing
A handbreadth, about four fingers wide
Fingerbreadths, a unit of measure
Empty space
Single books of the Torah, each written as its own scroll
Thumb, the width of a thumb

phrases.english: The measure of the margin: at the bottom, a handbreadth;
at the top, three fingerbreadths;
and between column and column —
a full space the width of two fingerbreadths;
and in separate books of the Torah, at the bottom, three fingerbreadths;
phrases.notes: This means a single חומש written as its own scroll, not a full ספר תורה.

phrases.english: at the top, two fingerbreadths;
and between column and column —
a full space the width of a thumb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving from columns to margins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a ספר תורה the margins are a טפח at the bottom, three fingers at the top, and two fingers between columns. In a single חומש they are three fingers, two fingers, and a thumb.

steps.title: Spaces between lines, words and letters
steps.stepSummary: The space between lines equals a line, between words a small letter, and between letters a hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between one line and the next, the height of a full line. Between one word and the next, the width of a small letter. Between one letter and the next, the width of a hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its layout rules with the smallest spaces on the page.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each kind of gap gets its own size. Lines need a lot of room, a full line's height. Words need enough room to look separate, about a small letter. Letters need only a hair's width, enough that they do not touch.

keyTerms.meaning: A line of writing
A word
A small letter, such as a י
A strand of hair, a tiny width

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא sets exact sizes for the whole page: columns per sheet, margins, and the spaces between lines, words and letters.

phrases.english: And between line and line, the size of a full line;

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין תֵּיבָה לְתֵיבָה כִּמְלֹא אוֹת קְטַנָּה,
phrases.english: and between word and word, the size of a small letter;

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין אוֹת לְאוֹת כִּמְלֹא חוּט הַשַּׂעֲרָה.
phrases.english: and between letter and letter, the width of a hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from margins down to spaces between lines, words and letters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Between lines, a line's height; between words, a small letter; between letters, a hair's width.

steps.title: Do not shrink the writing to save the required spaces
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that a scribe may not make his letters smaller just to keep the proper bottom margin, top margin, space between lines, or space between פרשיות.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person should not make his writing smaller, whether for the bottom space, the top space, the space between lines, or the space between one פרשה and the next.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a limit to the spacing rules it just gave: the spaces matter, but you may not get them by squeezing the letters smaller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 26-27 set required sizes for margins and gaps. A scribe running out of room might be tempted to write smaller letters to fit everything in. The ברייתא lists all four kinds of space and forbids shrinking the writing for any of them, so the writing must stay even in size.

keyTerms.meaning: Make smaller, reduce
The writing, the letters
Space, blank gap
A line of writing
A section or passage of the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel the margin rules from the earlier steps. The spaces are still required. The scribe just has to plan ahead so he can keep them without shrinking his letters.

phrases.english: A person should not make the writing smaller,
not for the sake of the space at the bottom,
and not for the sake of the space at the top,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִפְּנֵי רֶיוַח שֶׁבֵּין שִׁיטָה לְשִׁיטָה,
phrases.english: and not for the sake of the space between one line and the next,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִפְּנֵי רֶיוַח שֶׁבֵּין פָּרָשָׁה לְפָרָשָׁה.
phrases.english: and not for the sake of the space between one passage and the next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts a limit on the spacing rules of steps 26-27: the spaces may not be kept by shrinking the letters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The size of the writing must stay the same. It may not be reduced to keep any of the required margins or gaps.

steps.title: A five-letter word may not be split into the margin
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins a new case: if a five-letter word does not fit in the line, the scribe may not write two letters inside the column and three in the margin.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he comes to a word of five letters, he should not write two letters inside the column and three outside the column.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to a new layout problem: what to do when a word reaches the end of a line and does not fully fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scribe might want to start the word inside the column and let the rest spill into the margin. The ברייתא forbids this particular split, two letters in and three out, where most of the word would end up outside the column. The ברייתא continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A word
Letters
Here: the written column
Outside the column, in the margin

phrases.aramaic: נִזְדַּמְּנָה לוֹ תֵּיבָה בַּת חָמֵשׁ אוֹתִיּוֹת –
phrases.english: If he came upon a word of five letters,
phrases.notes: He means a word that reaches the end of the line and does not fully fit.

phrases.english: he should not write two letters inside the column
and three letters outside the column,

steps.triggerLanguage: נִזְדַּמְּנָה לוֹ תֵּיבָה בַּת חָמֵשׁ אוֹתִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא about layout, moving from spaces to words that run past the end of a line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A five-letter word may not be split with two letters inside the column and three letters in the margin.
